title: Non-blocking findings from backend-ibkr-symbol-resolution's review (PR #263)
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's review of PR #263 (backend-ibkr-symbol-resolution), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so it isn't lost once that PR merges. The PR itself has no blocking findings -- all tests pass (1157 passed, 99.95% coverage), mypy/ruff are clean on the touched files, no live network calls appear anywhere in the new tests, both 'decide X' checklist items have corresponding decisions entries, and the documented /iserver/secdef/search shape is internally consistent with how the rest of ibkr_provider.py already parses similar responses (reuses the existing _int_or_none helper the same way _parse_scanner_results does).

checklist.step: IBKRProvider.resolve_conid returns `int | None`, but IBKRProvider.get_hourly_bars takes `conid: str`. Confirmed with a standalone mypy check that `get_hourly_bars(resolve_conid(ticker), ...)` -- the exact composition this task's own description frames resolve_conid as unblocking ('get_hourly_bars/run_scanner both key off IBKR's own numeric conid... this task closes that gap') -- fails static type-checking today (`Argument 1 to "get_hourly_bars" ... has incompatible type "int"; expected "str"`). Not blocking this PR since resolve_conid isn't wired into any consumer yet (nothing exercises the composition), but the very next task that wires ticker-driven get_hourly_bars/run_scanner calls through resolve_conid will hit this immediately. Reconcile the conid type across the class (e.g. make get_hourly_bars accept `int | str`, or standardize on one representation and convert at the call boundary) before or as part of that wiring task.
